name: SoFi
payout: Research: $100–$150 per qualifying lead; directory lists an annual cap. Confirm the qualifying action.
why: Our audience is opening their first real savings and checking accounts, and SoFi is a chartered, FDIC-member bank with no account fees, which matches what we teach: keep savings insured and fee-free. We already have an in-depth review and a high-yield savings guide that explain SoFi's direct-deposit rate condition clearly, so readers who sign up know what to expect.
promo: SoFi appears in our SoFi Checking and Savings review, our high-yield savings comparison and our student bank account guide, plus short videos on emergency funds and moving savings out of 0.01% accounts.
compliance: We'll state the APY conditions and 'Member FDIC' exactly as you specify, date any rate we mention and link to your current terms.

name: CIT Bank
apply: https://www.cj.com/publisher (then apply to CIT Bank in the CJ marketplace)
payout: Research: about $100 per order. Confirm in CJ.
why: We teach readers to keep their emergency fund in a separate, FDIC-insured high-yield account. CIT Platinum Savings is a strong fit for readers who've reached a $5,000 balance, and our review explains the balance tier honestly, which means fewer surprised customers.
promo: CIT appears in our CIT Bank review, our high-yield savings comparison and our HYSA vs money market guide, and in emergency-fund videos aimed at people who've hit their first $5,000.
compliance: Rates are always dated, with a link to CIT's current rate table; we name First Citizens Bank as the FDIC member.

name: Ally Bank
apply: https://www.cj.com/publisher (apply to Ally in the CJ marketplace)
payout: Research lists Ally Invest at $25–$50 per sale; banking offers vary. Confirm in CJ.
why: Ally's savings buckets are the easiest way to run the sinking-funds method we teach, and the no-minimum, no-fee account fits students and early-career savers. We have a dedicated review and feature Ally in our savings comparisons.
promo: Ally appears in our Ally Bank review, savings comparisons and student bank account guide, and in videos about sinking funds and saving for several goals at once.
compliance: Banking content only unless approved for Ally Invest; any investing mention would carry your required broker disclosures.

name: Rocket Money
payout: Research: about $4–$10 per action. Confirm in Impact.
why: Finding and cancelling forgotten subscriptions is one of our most popular topics. Our Rocket Money review recommends starting with your free tier, which lowers the barrier to sign-up and builds trust before any Premium upgrade.
promo: Rocket Money appears in our full review, our budgeting apps comparison and our subscription audit guide, and in short videos on subscription audits, which we post every month.
compliance: We describe bill negotiation fees and Premium pricing accurately, as a range, linking to your pricing page.

name: Monarch Money
network: FlexOffers (Monarch also runs a partner team)
payout: Not published. Check FlexOffers / Impact listing.
why: Our readers are choosing their first paid budgeting app and comparing Monarch with YNAB. We publish a full Monarch review and a Monarch vs YNAB comparison that recommends Monarch for couples and people with accounts at several banks.
promo: Monarch appears in our review, our Monarch vs YNAB comparison and our budgeting apps guide, and in videos for couples managing money together.

name: YNAB
payout: Invite-based / by application. Terms in the program.
why: We teach zero-based budgeting and sinking funds, which is the YNAB method. Our YNAB review and comparisons point readers to the 34-day trial and the free year for college students, so the people who sign up are a good fit and more likely to stay.
promo: YNAB appears in our YNAB review, Monarch vs YNAB, the budgeting apps guide and 1099 Money's irregular-income budgeting posts.
tips: YNAB favours creators who already teach the method. Link to the YNAB review and a sinking-funds post in the application.

name: Empower Personal Dashboard
payout: Research: about $115 per qualifying lead. Confirm the qualifying action.
why: We teach readers to check the fees in their old 401(k)s and track net worth. The free dashboard's fee analyser is the tool we point to, in a dedicated review and our budgeting apps comparison.
promo: Empower appears in our Empower review, the budgeting apps guide and videos on 401(k) fees and net worth.
compliance: Empower is an SEC-registered adviser. We include 'Investing involves risk, including loss of principal', describe the advisory upsell accurately and will follow any review process you require.

name: Aura
payout: Research: $65 per enrollment (page metadata says up to $125). Net-30.
why: Scam Decoded's audience is actively worried about identity theft, often on behalf of parents. We recommend free steps first (credit freezes, two-factor login) and then Aura for families who want monitoring, insurance and a team to call, which brings you motivated, well-informed sign-ups.
promo: Aura appears in Scam Decoded's identity protection posts and Money Made Simple's Aura review and credit-freeze guide.
compliance: We describe insurance limits as 'up to' with your policy terms linked, and never use fear-based or 'you've been hacked' hooks.

name: Acorns
why: We reach complete beginners who've never invested, which is Acorns' core user. Our review recommends Acorns to people who'll add recurring deposits on top of round-ups, the users who stay longest.
promo: Acorns appears in our Acorns review and beginner investing posts.
compliance: We include 'Investing involves risk, including loss of principal' and Acorns' adviser disclosure, show fees accurately and will submit scripts for pre-approval.

name: Betterment
payout: Research: $25–$1,250 per referral, tiered by deposit.
why: We teach low-cost, diversified index investing for beginners. Our Betterment review and robo-adviser comparison explain the fee and recurring-deposit condition clearly, which attracts people who'll invest regularly.
promo: Betterment appears in our Betterment review, robo-adviser comparison and Roth IRA guide, and in 1099 Money's posts on retirement accounts for freelancers.
compliance: We understand the SEC Marketing Rule: we disclose compensation, include your required disclosures and Form CRS link, and will sign a written agreement and pre-clear content.

name: M1 Finance
why: Our audience is opening a first brokerage account or IRA and wants automatic, low-cost investing.
promo: Inclusion in investing comparisons and Roth IRA content once approved, with scripts sent to you first.
compliance: FINRA Rule 2210 applies: all content would be fair and balanced with no performance claims, and we'll submit every script for your pre-approval.
tips: M1 was fined by FINRA in 2024 over influencer content, so expect a strict review. Apply only once investing content has been live for a while.

name: Robinhood
apply: https://impact.com/partners/ (or email creators@robinhood.com once on Impact)
payout: Research: $5 per lead to $20 per funded account; figures inconsistent.
why: Beginner investors in our audience often ask about no-commission brokerages for buying index funds in a Roth IRA.
promo: Only in comparisons of where to open an IRA, focused on index funds, never trading or options.
compliance: FINRA 2210 applies. Scripts would be pre-approved. We don't cover options, crypto or individual stocks.
tips: Lower fit than others because of our no-trading rule; apply last.

why: Readers who already bank with Ally (from our Ally review) often want their first IRA in the same place.
promo: Roth IRA and beginner investing guides.
compliance: Broker disclosures included; FINRA 2210 fair-and-balanced standard; scripts pre-cleared.

name: FreeTaxUSA
why: We publish tax-season content every January to April for students, early-career workers and freelancers. Our review and tax software comparison recommend FreeTaxUSA because the federal return is free even with 1099 income, a strong match for both Money Made Simple and 1099 Money.
promo: FreeTaxUSA appears in our FreeTaxUSA review, our tax software comparison and 1099 Money's filing-season posts, with a newsletter feature in late January.
compliance: We always mention VITA and IRS Free File for people who qualify, and describe state fees accurately.

name: TaxAct
why: Freelancers in our audience need software that handles Schedule C and quarterly estimates; TaxAct sits in our tax software comparison as an option with more guided support.
promo: Tax software comparison, 1099 Money's January–April filing content and quarterly tax reminders.
compliance: We describe what each tier covers and never imply a free tier covers forms it doesn't.

name: Self Financial
why: Building credit from zero is a core topic for both Money Made Simple and Dinero Simple, whose audience includes many first-generation and new-to-credit adults. Our review explains exactly how the credit builder works and its cost, so sign-ups are informed.
promo: Self appears in our Self review, credit-score explainers and Dinero Simple's Spanish credit-building series.
compliance: We show the fee and APR, warn that late payments are reported, and present alternatives such as secured cards.

name: Kikoff
why: Kikoff is a low-cost credit-building option for our new-to-credit audience, listed in our credit-builder comparisons.
promo: Credit-building comparisons and Dinero Simple's credit series.

name: Chime
why: Students and early-career workers in our audience want fee-free checking without overdraft fees; Chime is in our student bank account guide.
promo: Student bank account guide, overdraft-fee videos and Dinero Simple's banking basics.
compliance: We state that Chime is a financial technology company, not a bank, and name the partner banks.

name: Remitly
why: Sending money to family abroad is one of Dinero Simple's most important topics. We teach viewers to compare the total cost, fee plus exchange rate, which suits a transparent provider.

compliance: We always show the total cost for a concrete example, never just 'no fee', and a native speaker reviews every post.

name: Wise
why: Dinero Simple viewers send money abroad and 1099 Money freelancers get paid by international clients; both care about the mid-market rate and transparent fees.
promo: Remittance comparisons (Dinero Simple) and 'getting paid by clients abroad' posts (1099 Money).
compliance: Total cost shown for a concrete example.

promo: 1099 Money's invoicing and bookkeeping posts, accounting-software comparisons and the newsletter's 'set up your business money' issues.

name: QuickBooks
